title: Sort by CPU, don't scan a wall of processes by eye
explanation: `top` (Shift+P to sort by `%CPU`) or `ps -eo pid,pcpu,comm --sort=-pcpu | head` puts the worst offender at the top immediately. On this box's single, deliberately tight 0.5 vCPU core, one process pinned near 100% explains the whole-box sluggishness directly -- there's no need to look further once you see it.

title: Confirm the exact process before acting
explanation: `pgrep -af report-generator` gives its PID and full command line. It's a plain retry loop with no sleep in it at all (`while true; do :; done`) -- there's no legitimate workload here to preserve, no config to tune, just a stuck loop burning cycles for no purpose.

title: Stop it, escalating only if needed
explanation: `sudo pkill -f report-generator` sends SIGTERM first, which is the polite default -- it gives the process a chance to exit cleanly if it happens to have any cleanup logic. Only reach for `kill -9` (SIGKILL) if it ignores TERM, since SIGKILL bypasses any chance for the process to shut down gracefully.

title: Verify against the same view that found it
explanation: `top` should now show the core idle instead of pinned. The durable fix, if this were a real recurring job rather than a training scenario, is in the program itself -- add a sleep or backoff so a retry loop never spins unbounded again -- but killing the stuck process is what restores the box right now.
